record.paper_title: Conjectures and Open Questions on the Structure and Regularity of Spaces with Lower Ricci Curvature Bounds
record.original_question: Let (M_i^n, g_i, ν_i, p_i) converge in the measured Gromov–Hausdorff sense to (X, d, ν, p), with Ric_i ≥ −λ and Vol(B_1(p_i)) → 0. If Theorem 3.1 gives a unique rectifiable dimension k for X, is the Hausdorff dimension of X equal to this same integer k?

evidence.quote: Theorem 3.1 (Cheeger–Colding [2], Colding–Naber [5]). Let Mni, gi, νi, pi → (X, d, ν, p) with Ric ≥ −λ and Vol(B1(pi)) → 0. Then there exists a unique k ≤ n such that X is k-rectifiable.
Open Problem 3.2. Show the Hausdorff dim of X is same as the rectifiable dimension k from Theorem 3.1.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Setup. Fix integers n ≥ 2 and a constant λ ≥ 0. Consider a sequence of pointed complete n-dimensional Riemannian manifolds (M_i^n, g_i, p_i) satisfying the lower Ricci curvature bound Ric_{g_i} ≥ −λ, equipped with their renormalized volume measures ν_i (i.e., ν_i = Vol_{g_i}/Vol_{g_i}(B_1(p_i))). Assume that

  (a) (M_i^n, g_i, ν_i, p_i) converges in the pointed measured Gromov–Hausdorff sense to a pointed metric measure space (X, d, ν, p), and
  (b) the sequence is collapsing in the sense that Vol_{g_i}(B_1(p_i)) → 0.

By a theorem of Cheeger–Colding and Colding–Naber, there exists a unique integer k with 1 ≤ k ≤ n such that X is k-rectifiable; that is, ν-almost every point of X has a unique tangent cone equal to ℝ^k, and X can be covered up to a ν-null set by countably many bi-Lipschitz images of subsets of ℝ^k.

Question. Is the Hausdorff dimension dim_H(X, d) of the limit space necessarily equal to this rectifiable dimension k?
artifact.status_search_result: Pan and Wei (Geometric and Functional Analysis, 2022; arXiv:2106.03967) resolved the question negatively. They constructed explicit collapsing Ricci limit spaces (universal covers of certain doubly warped products [0,∞) ×_f S^{p−1} ×_h S^1 with h(r) ~ r^{−β}) for which the Hausdorff dimension equals 1+β and can be a non-integer strictly larger than the rectifiable dimension k. Hence Hausdorff dimension need not equal the rectifiable integer k.

status_evidence.title: Examples of Ricci limit spaces with non-integer Hausdorff dimension
status_evidence.snippet: Pan and Wei give the first examples of collapsing Ricci limit spaces where the Hausdorff dimension of the singular set exceeds that of the regular set, and the Hausdorff dimension can be non-integer.
status_evidence.claim: Hausdorff dimension of a collapsed Ricci limit space can be a non-integer strictly larger than the rectifiable dimension k, disproving equality.

status_evidence.title: Examples of Ricci limit spaces with non-integer Hausdorff dimension – GAFA
status_evidence.snippet: Published in Geometric and Functional Analysis, vol. 32 (2022), pp. 676–685.
status_evidence.claim: The negative resolution is published in a peer-reviewed journal.
